terms.definition: The rigid outer layer of plant, fungal, and many bacterial cells that supports and protects the cell.
terms.function: Gives the cell its fixed shape and protects it.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets plants stand tall and keeps plant cells strong.

terms.definition: The tough carbohydrate that forms the plant cell wall.
terms.whereItIs: Woven through the plant cell wall.
terms.whyItMatters: Cellulose is what makes wood strong.

terms.definition: A small opening in the cell wall that lets water and materials pass through.
terms.function: Allows water and dissolved molecules to reach the membrane.
terms.whyItMatters: The wall supports but does not block the cell's traffic.

terms.definition: The outward pressure of the water-filled vacuole pressing against the cell wall.
terms.whereItIs: Inside plant cells, between vacuole and wall.
terms.whyItMatters: Together with the wall it is why plants stay upright.
